editorial:
Ever wondered about the weirdest stories in religious history? You get a look at some wild tales here, like a monk who could actually fly and a man who kept talking after his head was cut off. It tries to frame these holy figures as the original superhumans, mixing faith with a bit of a freak-show vibe. The setup sounds like a great ride for anyone into myths and legends, but the mood feels a bit off from the start because the narrator doesn't seem to actually like the subject matter.

You will quickly notice some big problems that make it hard to enjoy. The voiceover is full of sarcasm and seems to be mocking the church, which might annoy you if you are looking for a serious documentary. To make things worse, the editing is messy; for example, you will see a picture of St. Anthony while the narrator is talking about St. Christopher. Because of these mistakes, it is hard to stay focused.
endingExplained: Since the film is a collection of stories rather than a plot, there is no big twist. It wraps up by trying to connect these ancient miracles to the idea of human potential. However, because the narrator is so critical of the church, the conclusion feels more like a critique of religion than a celebration of the saints. It ends on a confusing note that leaves you wondering if the filmmaker actually believed anything he said.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves debunking myths or spotting bad editing.
